Lorsqu’on est jeune, grandir à Saint-Léo: Growing up in Saint-Léonard in today’s Montréal can be a challenge for young people, especially if you belong to a visible minority community. It becomes easier to make it through when you have success stories from the “hood” to look up to, role models like Freakey!.
Ayant vécu à Saint-Léonard depuis aussi: Freakey! has lived in Saint-Léonard for as long as he can remember. He is a music producer and composer who works with artists in Europe and the United States. He goes by that name because he considers himself “a little weird, a little different, and [his] music, like him, is too.” More than six years after his first musical success, he hasn’t left the neighbourhood that watched him grow up.
« J’ai développé l’amour de la musique à: “I fell in love with music at 12. I started taking it seriously around 14,” he explains. That interest in music created a kind of protective “bubble” around him. “By surrounding myself with good people, I managed to make a dream I’d had since my teens come true,” says the Montrealer. “When I was a teenager, making music was an escape from the problems I had.”
Si l’entourage et les fréquentations jou: While he sees the people around him and the company he keeps as crucial, he also considers himself lucky to have grown up in an environment where those close to him never stopped encouraging him. “I have a really good relationship with my family. In a way, it’s thanks to my parents that I’m where I am today.”
Lorsqu’il entre dans l’adolescence, ses: When he entered adolescence, his pastimes often revolved around music. “At one point, all I asked for was things related to music. My parents got fed up. Then they realized that if I stayed home and gave it everything I had, it kept me from hanging around outside and picking up bad habits. In my music, I was in my own world.”
Au début, ses parents avaient des réserv: At first, his parents had reservations. “They weren’t too keen on the idea. When I told them I wanted to make music, they saw it more as a hobby than a career,” the artist recalls. “Over time, they saw that I was really committed and that I was taking it seriously. They figured that by helping me down this path, it could keep me away from the wrong one, that it kept me busy and at home.”

Né à Montréal, le producteur ne cache pa: Born in Montréal, the producer makes no secret of his love for his culture of origin. “I’ve always been very proud to be Haitian. This culture brings something new, something fresh to Montréal. And I’m proud to contribute to that with what I do,” he says. “I’m really happy when I see that the Haitian community has stepped outside and come to enrich Montréal’s culture,” he continues.
« Ma culture d’origine a toujours occupé: “My culture of origin has always taken up a big place in my life.” His cultural heritage has also greatly influenced his career. “Ever since I was little, we’ve listened to music at home. I got interested in it super young and, as far back as I can remember, I fell in love with it at first contact.” He says that “Haitian culture brings something flavourful, not only to [his] life, but to everything it touches musically and culturally.”
Le producteur de musique montréalais a t: The Montréal music producer has always lived in the same neighbourhood. “My whole life is in Saint-Léonard,” he will repeat several times. This sense of belonging comes from his childhood in the neighbourhood and all the memories tied to it. “I went to elementary school there, I was always out and about when I was younger. I grew up there, I evolved there – and I’m still evolving there today. It’s a part of me,” he continues.
Plus jeune, il n’a pas eu beaucoup de mo: When he was younger, he didn’t have many role models from the neighbourhood – even fewer in music production. “When I started out, I looked up to people like Southside and Young Chop. They’re all from the United States. Coming from Saint-Léonard and having my own sound, my own music, that matters. I want to influence younger people the same way Southside and Young Chop influenced me,” he explains.
Sa carrière se développe doucement jusqu: His career developed slowly until he was 19, when his destiny changed overnight. “A friend had started rapping. He was also a guy from Saint-Léonard; we’ve known each other since we were little kids. I was working a lot with him, and he was starting to get more well known in Europe,” he says. “Then one day, randomly and on the spur of the moment, I sent a message on Instagram to a hugely popular rapper in Europe – Hamza, a Belgian rapper – with a beat I’d prepared. The next day, I was stunned: he had replied and even sent me back a song using what I’d sent him. He liked what I’d cooked up, and after that song, my life and my career changed dramatically.”
Si le producteur a su se concentrer sur: While the producer was able to stay focused on his passion, finding his place hasn’t always been easy. He attended a specialized high school for young people with behavioural difficulties. The school is in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, a few kilometres away.
« Je n’étais pas bon à l’école », affirm: “I wasn’t good at school,” he says with a small laugh. “Academically, it was a disaster. They put me in a class for kids with behavioural problems, and it made me feel like I was bad and different.” Today, he believes he had more problems with concentration than with behaviour. Even so, he says he is “happy with how things turned out for him.” Playful and sociable by nature, Freakey! recalls with a laugh that he was “goofy” in class and with his friends.
Lorsqu’il commence à s’investir à fond d: When he started throwing himself fully into his production, around age 18, his main obstacle was his lack of financial resources. “I put everything into my music. I saw guys around me making easy money, others working honestly part-time or full-time; me, I was working for myself. It was hard. I had to believe in myself and in what I wanted, because I was dependent, I couldn’t afford to fail,” he explains.
« J’ai eu de la chance, je me suis entou: “I was lucky, I surrounded myself with a good group of people. It helped me a lot, because even if that wasn’t the case at the beginning, the people close to me who believed in me helped me not give up and keep going.” He lets out a small smile before adding: “When you’re a musician or an artist, you have no choice: you have to stay focused and disciplined. It can be hard at first, but when you succeed, you become a stronger person.”
Alors qu’il commence à se faire connaîtr: Just as he was beginning to make a name for himself in the industry, the death of his grandmother deeply affected him. “The year she left us was very hard. I was super close to her. When I made music, I didn’t necessarily expect her to encourage me, I just appreciated having her near me. She motivated me, pushed me. When I lost her, I stepped back and needed time before getting back to my art,” he says.
Freakey! encourage les jeunes à s’engage: Freakey! encourages young people to get into music production, a field where building a career is becoming more realistic, and which also offers an escape from the problems of violence in disadvantaged neighbourhoods. “I want young people to be able to look at me and tell themselves that you have to take the right path in life. I want to give the younger ones who are watching me the strength and motivation to achieve everything they want by making the right choices, avoiding the traps and the violence tied to street problems,” he continues.
Il revient à plusieurs reprises sur la q: He comes back several times to the question of perseverance. “If you want to make a living from your music, it’s possible. You just have to bet everything on yourself and be able to discipline yourself. That’s all it is.”
Selon lui, il est capital de se vouer en: In his view, it is essential to devote yourself entirely to your passion. “If I have a message for young people, it would be not to hesitate to make sacrifices for what you truly want. Staying shut in with my music equipment instead of hanging out outside, cutting off bad company, dedicating time – entire nights and days! – to my passion, those are sacrifices that seem enormous when you’re young. But in the end, when you’re inspired, it’s the best gift you can give yourself,” he adds dreamily.
Aujourd’hui encore, lorsque Freakey! app: Even today, when Freakey! appears on stage alongside other artists, you recognize him by the singularity of his persona: it’s hard to miss his eccentric look and his energy, which he calls “weird.” If you look at the music culture of the city, hip-hop in particular, it is impossible to overlook this producer. He wants young people to be able to believe in their ambitions without their living conditions getting in the way of achieving their dreams. And for that, “we need more people from the hood who succeed and who can give back to their neighbourhoods. As time goes on, we also have to tell ourselves that we’re condemned to excellence,” he concludes.
